J1.evidence: (1) The book introduces al-Maʿarrī's line with «أولم يقل لهم مخاطبا: غدوت مريض العقل والدين فالقني», i.e. addressed to them (غدوتَ = you have become sick in intellect and religion, so meet me); EN renders 'I became sick in intellect and religion', contradicting its own 'addressing them'. (2) «بالذي ألهم تعذيبي ... ثناياك العذابا»: ألهم takes ثناياك as object and تعذيبي as second object, العذابا (sweet) qualifying ثناياك = 'by Him who inspired your sweet front teeth to torment me'; EN 'who inspired my torment, [and made] your teeth sweet and cool' breaks the syntax and adds an unmarked bracket '[and made]'. Wrong meaning.

J2.evidence: (1) Maʿarrī: the author introduces the line with «أولم يقل لهم مخاطبا» and the verse itself has the imperative «فالقني», so «غدوت مريض العقل والدين» is second person (ghadawta: you have become sick in mind and religion, so meet me); EN 'I became sick in intellect and religion; so meet me' inverts the addressee and contradicts 'addressing them'. (2) al-Ṣūrī: «بالذي ألهم تعذيبي ثناياك العذابا» = by Him who inspired your sweet (العذاب) front teeth (ثناياك, 1st object of ألهم) with tormenting me (تعذيبي, 2nd object); EN 'who inspired my torment, [and made] your teeth sweet and cool' breaks the double-object structure and inserts an unmarked bracketed verb '[and made]'. Both need fixing.

J1.evidence: Arabic «ونسبهما في الكامل لأبي دلف» does not name the author of al-Kamil. The Turkish '[Müberred] el-Kâmil'de' adds the attribution in plain square brackets, which is an unmarked addition. Likewise «والروح العلائية معروفة» becomes 'Alâî ruh [Ebü'l-Alâ'nın ruhu]', and «يعزيه بالرشيد» becomes 'Reşîd ['in vefatı] için'. These are interpretive additions that are not inside «[Mütercim notu: …]». They must be moved into such notes. The rest of the Turkish is faithful.

J2.evidence: Arabic «ونسبهما في الكامل لأبي دلف» names no author, but the Turkish writes '[Müberred] el-Kâmil'de'; «والروح العلائية معروفة» becomes 'Alâî ruh [Ebü'l-Alâ'nın ruhu]'; and the Ebû Nüvâs line gets 'Reşîd ['in vefatı]'. These are interpretive additions in bare square brackets, not inside [Mütercim notu: ...]. The Turkish also has other bare-bracket supplements (e.g. [Yûnus], [hilafetini], [bu oklar]) that need the same check. Fix: put the identifications and glosses inside Mütercim notu. The rest of the translation looked faithful.

J1.evidence: «ونص أصحابنا على أن كم الاستفهامية والخبرية لا توصف ولا يوصف بها» = our colleagues stated explicitly that كم is neither qualified nor used as a qualifier. TR «...«كم»in ne sıfatlanacağını ne de onunla sıfat yapılacağını açıkça belirtmişlerdir»: in Turkish ne...ne de with the main predicate negates belirtmek, giving 'they stated explicitly neither that it is qualified nor that...', i.e. silence instead of an explicit prohibition. Should read e.g. «...sıfatlanmadığını ve onunla sıfat yapılmadığını açıkça belirtmişlerdir». Also «(Cümlenin)» before «قرن»in sıfatı is an unmarked addition (source just «ويجوز أن يكون صفة لقرن»).

J2.evidence: Arabic «ونص أصحابنا على أن كم الاستفهامية والخبرية لا توصف ولا يوصف بها» = our colleagues explicitly stated that كم (interrogative and khabariyya) is NOT qualified and NOT used as a qualifier (an objection to Zamakhsharī's صفة analysis). TR 'ne sıfatlanacağını ne de onunla sıfat yapılacağını açıkça belirtmişlerdir': in Turkish 'ne X ne de Y' + verb negates the verb for each object (cf. 'ne kitabı ne de defteri okudum'), so it reads 'they stated neither that it is qualified nor that it qualifies' - the negation moves from the content to the act of stating, reversing the point. Should be e.g. 'sıfatlanmayacağını ve onunla sıfat yapılmayacağını açıkça belirtmişlerdir'.
